title: Differentiation, optimization and tensor programs
approval: Author-agent design review; not scientific acceptance or publication approval.

figures.title: Shapes are part of the equation
figures.mechanism: Matrix multiply, broadcast, tanh, project, score
figures.captionThesis: Every operation has an explicit shape and a reverse counterpart.
figures.misleadingInterpretation: Equal shapes do not guarantee correct semantics.

figures.title: Reverse accumulation is local accounting
figures.readerQuestion: How do all parameters receive gradients?
figures.mechanism: Seed scalar loss with one and propagate vector-Jacobian products
figures.captionThesis: Reused values receive the sum of all downstream contributions.
figures.misleadingInterpretation: A computation DAG is not necessarily the model's information-flow guarantee.

figures.title: Three routes to the same derivative
figures.readerQuestion: What makes a gradient check meaningful?
figures.mechanism: Compute all three, scan step sizes, expose intentional failure
figures.captionThesis: Agreement at smooth finite inputs is evidence with a stated scope.
figures.misleadingInterpretation: Agreement does not prove the objective or dataset is correct.

figures.title: Correct gradients can still diverge
figures.readerQuestion: Why can a gradient step increase loss?
figures.mechanism: Compare eta lambda below, equal to, and above two
figures.captionThesis: The gradient is local information; step size determines stability.
figures.misleadingInterpretation: One stable quadratic is not convergence evidence for a neural architecture.

figures.title: Broadcast backward is a sum
figures.readerQuestion: Where does a shared bias collect contributions?
figures.mechanism: Accumulate row contributions onto one parameter
figures.captionThesis: Forward sharing requires reverse summation, not arbitrary averaging.
figures.misleadingInterpretation: Loss normalization and broadcast reduction are separate operations.

figures.title: Stable softmax cross entropy
figures.mechanism: Subtract row maximum before exponentiating; compare equivalent objectives
figures.captionThesis: Algebraic equality does not imply numerical equality.
figures.evidenceSource: PyTorch numerical accuracy and CrossEntropyLoss; original examples
figures.misleadingInterpretation: Stability is not immunity to all nonfinite inputs.

figures.title: Repeated backward calls accumulate
figures.mechanism: Accumulate sums then normalize once using the declared denominator
figures.captionThesis: Batch weighting must match the objective from Chapter 2.
figures.misleadingInterpretation: Equal averaging of unequal batches changes the loss.

figures.title: Roundoff competes with truncation
figures.readerQuestion: Why not use an arbitrarily tiny finite-difference step?
figures.mechanism: Sweep powers of ten against a smooth analytic derivative
figures.captionThesis: The useful h range depends on scale and precision.
figures.evidenceSource: Original Taylor derivation; PyTorch numerical accuracy
figures.misleadingInterpretation: A specific optimum is not portable across dtypes and functions.

figures.title: Differentiating a selected computation
figures.mechanism: Separate selected-branch derivatives from selection changes
figures.captionThesis: Autograd of the executed branch is not a derivative through arbitrary discrete choices.
figures.misleadingInterpretation: No claim that genomic structural search is solved by ordinary backprop.

figures.title: Objective, gradient and update are distinct
figures.readerQuestion: Where do optimizer state and regularization enter?
figures.mechanism: Track state before and after one declared optimizer step
figures.captionThesis: An update rule adds semantics beyond differentiation.
figures.evidenceSource: PyTorch SGD; optimizer sources to expand before publication
figures.misleadingInterpretation: Do not mix coupled L2 and decoupled decay formulas.

figures.title: A gradient test needs a controlled computation
figures.mechanism: Hold state fixed; perturb just one coordinate; restore inputs
figures.captionThesis: Numerical checks compare the same function only under controlled conditions.
figures.misleadingInterpretation: Finite checks are neither general causality proofs nor universal numerical certification.

figures.title: From a local update to a reproducible training run
figures.mechanism: Compose verified local semantics with a controlled training lifecycle
figures.captionThesis: A validated tiny update is not an experiment demonstrating generalization.
figures.misleadingInterpretation: No DOGMA/Hermon training or engine claim.
